column1: # Exact per-file ownership-verifier expectations for the direct-call carrier
# corpus. Columns: fixture, under-release findings, other blocking MIR findings,
# `hew check` exit code, runtime mode. Every finding is blocking.
# Runtime modes and what each one proves:
#   check   the fixture is checked only (no `main` to execute, or a module root).
#   clean   the fixture is BUILT at -O2 and executed under the platform leak
#           oracle, and must report ZERO leaks.
#   refuse  the fixture must produce a blocking MIR finding and a non-zero exit.
# Every executed fixture drives its shape at least 200,000 times. A per-call
# residue of one allocation is invisible at a single iteration, and refcounted
# shares of one string collapse into a single leak node — an executed fixture
# that calls its shape once can report zero leaks while leaking on every call.
# pO_alias.hew pins the fixed move-chain case: a discarded owned item yielded by
# a `VecIter` transfers its release obligation to the terminal local and is
# vec_iter_temp_receiver.hew pins the caller half of the by-value cursor ABI: a
# terminal or adapter called straight on `.into_iter()` relinquishes its
# temporary at the call, so the callee's release is the only one.
